# CPU1 (Cortex-M33) first-party warning-profile escape inventory -- issue #843.
#
# Each row is a FIRST-PARTY translation unit on a CPU1 executable that
# ra8_add_cpu1_image()'s per-source profile (-Wall -Wextra -Werror ...
# -Wstack-usage=2048 -fstack-usage) never reaches: it compiles at
# -mcpu=cortex-m33 ... -Os with no warning flags and emits no .su stack data.
# These are the sources #843 must bring onto the bar. Two ways a TU lands here:
#
#   * the app bolts it onto a helper-built image with its own target_sources(),
#     and the helper scopes the profile to its own SOURCES (compile_on_m33,
#     ereader_m33);
#   * the app HAND-ROLLS the CPU1 executable with add_executable() plus its own
#     -mcpu=cortex-m33 options and never calls the helper, so NOTHING on that
#     image carries the profile, its own cpu1_main.c included (cpu1_pingpong,
#     cpu1_pingpong_ipc).
#
# Format: <cpu1-target>  <repo-relative source path>
#
# scripts/checks/check_cpu1_warning_profile.py judges this file. The list is
# SHRINK-ONLY: a first-party CPU1 source that is not here fails the gate, and a
# row that stops escaping (profile-covered, detached from the image, or deleted)
# fails as stale and must be removed. Never add a row to silence a new escape
# without saying why in review. Vendored SOUP never belongs here: it is
# deliberately outside the first-party bar and the gate rejects such a row.
#
# A missing, unreadable or empty file yields the EMPTY set, so every escape
# reports. The gate fails closed.
